headline: SIGMA LITHIUM Shares Crater 15% After Brazilian Court Orders Halt to Waste Disposal at Grota do Cirilo
snippet: A local Aracuaí court ruled May 17 that Sigma Lithium must halt waste pile operations at its flagship Brazilian lithium operation, citing earlier environmental violations. Shares dropped 15% before the company launched an appeal, calling the ruling unwarranted; similar Brazilian cases typically take years to resolve and no payment is currently due.

headline: GOLD HITS 7-WEEK LOW AT $4,481, Then Rallies — Silver Rebounds Above $78 on US-Iran Sanctions Pause Rumour
snippet: Gold fell to its lowest since late March before recovering 1.2% Monday after Tehran media reported the US offered to pause Iranian oil sanctions during Pakistan-mediated peace talks. Silver clawed back from an 8-session low below $74 to above $78 per ounce on the same headline; the G7 finance ministers also met to discuss the government bond selloff.

headline: CRITICAL METALS Snaps Up European Lithium at 113% Premium to Consolidate Full Tanbreez Ownership
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML) signed a binding scheme agreement May 18 to acquire European Lithium's remaining 7.5% stake in the Tanbreez project in Greenland, one of the world's largest rare earth and lithium deposits. The all-stock deal values each European Lithium share at A$0.58 — a 113% premium to the 20-day VWAP — and is expected to close in H2 2026.

headline: Royal Gold Swaps Hod Maden Equity for Royalty — Cuts Stake from 30% to 15%, Collects New 2.5% NSR
snippet: Royal Gold (NASDAQ: RGLD) announced May 17 it is cutting its direct equity in Turkey's Hod Maden gold-copper project from 30% to 15% while receiving a new 2.5% net smelter return royalty. The restructuring strips future capital cost exposure from Royal Gold as SSR Mining simultaneously exits its 20% stake and receives a 4.0% NSR.

headline: DAKOTA GOLD Drills 1.42 g/t Over 64 Metres at Richmond Hill — Heap-Leach PFS Due H2 2026
snippet: Dakota Gold's 2026 infill campaign at its South Dakota heap-leach project returned 1.42 g/t Au and 5.97 g/t Ag over 64.0 metres, boosting confidence in the resource model ahead of a Pre-Feasibility Study expected in the second half of 2026. The 109-hole, 15,481-metre programme includes infill, expansion and geotechnical drilling.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD Buys Orla Mining for US$5.1B — Combined Entity Becomes Canada's Second-Largest Gold Producer
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining announced a US$5.1 billion all-stock merger on May 13 that creates an US$18.5 billion producer with six operating mines across Canada, the US, Nicaragua and Mexico targeting over one million ounces annually. Backed by industry veteran Pierre Lassonde, the deal requires shareholder votes expected in July and is set to close in Q3 2026.

headline: NGEX MINERALS Hits 17.3m at 207.79 g/t Gold at Lunahuasi — Bonanza Zone 660 Metres From Previous Record Intercept
snippet: NGEx Minerals (TSX: NGEX) released Phase 4 drill results May 13 showing 17.3 metres at 207.79 g/t gold at its Lunahuasi copper-gold deposit in Argentina, including a 2.0-metre bonanza intercept at 1,740 g/t. The high-grade vein zone sits 660 metres from a previous record hole, demonstrating the deposit's exceptional spatial extent.

headline: NEXGEN ENERGY Targets Summer 2026 Construction Start at Rook I — Canada's Biggest Uranium Deposit Ever to Be Built
snippet: NexGen Energy made its Final Investment Decision following the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission's March federal approval, targeting summer 2026 as the start of a four-year construction programme at Rook I in northern Saskatchewan. At full production, the mine is capable of supplying over 20% of current global uranium demand — roughly 30 million pounds per year.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Revives Lithium Demand — Morgan Stanley Sees 80,000-Tonne LCE Deficit in 2026
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery storage is tightening the lithium market faster than most models predicted. Morgan Stanley projects an 80,000-tonne lithium carbonate equivalent deficit in 2026 as energy storage rises to 31% of total consumption, up from 23% in 2025 — bolstering hopes for a lasting price recovery after three years of oversupply.

headline: GDX IS UP 70% From 2025's Average — Gold Stocks Are Finally Outrunning the Metal
snippet: Gold miners tracked by GDX have averaged $97.79 year-to-date — 69.6% above their 2025 average — as higher gold prices translate directly into expanded margins and earnings. The analysis argues the structural revaluation has further room to run even amid near-term corrections, with gold stocks still historically undervalued relative to bullion.

headline: GOLD FELL ON HOT CPI. Here's the Mechanism Most Investors Miss — and Why $6,000 Isn't Off the Table
snippet: Gold has corrected 16% from its January $5,589 all-time high despite US inflation rising to 3.8% — the highest since 2023. The counterintuitive drop is driven by Fed rate-hike expectations, not inflation itself. If the Hormuz conflict resolves and oil falls back, analysts see gold re-testing $5,000 rapidly with a pathway to $6,000 by year-end.

headline: COPPER FACES TARIFF WILDCARD — US Commerce Report Due June 30 Could Set 15–30% Duty on Refined Imports
snippet: The US Commerce Secretary must deliver a Section 232 copper market report to the President by June 30, 2026, potentially triggering tariffs of 15% from 2027 rising to 30% from 2028 on refined copper imports. Miners of ores and concentrates remain exempt from the existing 50% tariff on semi-finished copper products, creating an investment angle for upstream producers.
